rics.description: BANKRUPTCY FILINGS, BUSINESS, CHAPTER 11 (QUARTERLY FILINGS)
rics.meaning: Chapter 11 business bankruptcy filings, quarterly.
rics.how_to_use: Reorganization filings. Big-cap Ch.11 cases (large notional debt) more market-relevant than counts.

rics.description: BANKRUPTCY FILINGS, TOTAL CHAPTER 11 (QUARTERLY FILINGS)
rics.meaning: Total Chapter 11 bankruptcy filings — corporate reorganizations under federal bankruptcy code. Companies filing here aim to restructure debt while continuing operations (vs Ch 7 liquidation).
rics.how_to_use: Cyclical late-cycle stress signal — peaks 6-12 months after recession start. Major filings (Hertz 2020, JCPenney 2020, SVB 2023) drive headline numbers but small-business filings give cleaner cycle signal. Pre-2008 norm ~3,000/quarter; post-2010 ~2,000/quarter.

rics.description: Bankruptcy filings (12 months ending), business, total
rics.meaning: Total business bankruptcy filings, rolling 12-month — Chapter 7 (liquidation) + Chapter 11 (reorg) + Chapter 13 + Chapter 12 (farm). Smoother than quarterly; better for cycle reads.
rics.how_to_use: 12-month rolling smooths volatility. Track YoY change for cycle signal: rising YoY indicates corporate stress accumulating. SBA-loan defaults flow into this stat with 6-9 month lag.

rics.description: Bankruptcy filings (12 months ending), non-business, total
rics.meaning: Total non-business (consumer/personal) bankruptcy filings, rolling 12-month — Chapter 7 + Chapter 13 personal filings. Larger volume than business filings (~400-500K/year vs ~25K/year).
rics.how_to_use: Consumer-stress gauge. Spiked 2003-05 (record 2M filings before reform), fell post-2005 BAPCPA reform, low post-2010. Watch alongside credit-card delinquencies — bankruptcies lag delinquencies by 6-12 months.

rics.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, agricultural loans
rics.meaning: Charge-off rate, all banks, agricultural loans — share of ag loans deemed uncollectible. Quarterly FDIC release. Small loan book (~$80B) but cyclically sensitive to commodity prices.
rics.how_to_use: Track for ag-cycle stress. Spikes when crop prices fall sharply (1986 farm crisis, 2015-16 commodity downturn). Currently low. Combined with ag-real-estate values, signals farm-sector financial health.

rics.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, commercial and industrial loans
rics.meaning: Bank charge-off rate, C&I loans.
rics.how_to_use: Business credit-loss gauge. Rises ~6-12 months after recession start.

rics.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, consumer loans, all
rics.meaning: Bank charge-off rate, total consumer loans.
rics.how_to_use: Consumer credit losses — leading sign of household stress.

rics.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, consumer loans, credit cards
rics.meaning: Bank Charge-off Rate, credit cards. Most pro-cyclical loan category.
rics.how_to_use: Crossing 4% historically signals recession-like consumer stress. Currently elevated, especially subprime. Card delinquencies (aUSBDLCOCQ/A) lead charge-offs by 3-6 months.

rics.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, consumer loans, other
rics.meaning: Charge-off rate, all banks, consumer loans (other) — auto loans + personal loans + other non-card consumer credit. Excludes credit cards (separate series) and mortgages.
rics.how_to_use: Auto-loan-driven mostly. Subprime auto charge-offs are the leading edge — rising ahead of broader consumer stress. Track alongside auto-loan-90+-day delinquencies (NY Fed) for triangulated read.

rics.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, leases
rics.meaning: Charge-off rate, all banks, leases — equipment leasing exposures. Smaller portfolio than C&I loans (~$120B at large banks).
rics.how_to_use: Cyclical with capex cycles. Equipment leases (cars, trucks, machinery) charge off in slowdowns when small businesses fail. Watch alongside C&I charge-offs for full business-credit quality picture.

rics.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, real estate loans, all
rics.meaning: Bank charge-off rate, real estate.
rics.how_to_use: Combined residential + CRE charge-offs. CRE-led elevation now.

rics.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, real estate loans, commercial
rics.meaning: Bank Charge-off Rate, CRE (commercial real estate). Heavy office/retail CRE losses post-COVID.
rics.how_to_use: Bank stress concentrated here for regional banks (large banks have less CRE exposure). Office is the worst sub-sector; multifamily improving; industrial healthy. Watch alongside CMBS spreads.

rics.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, real estate loans, residential
rics.meaning: Bank charge-off rate, residential real estate.
rics.how_to_use: Mortgage charge-offs — historically low (mortgage credit standards strict post-2008).

rics.description: Charge-Off rates, all banks, total loans and leases
rics.meaning: Total Bank Charge-off Rate, all loans and leases. Aggregate bank-credit-loss gauge from FDIC quarterly.
rics.how_to_use: Counter-cyclical: rises ~6-12 months after recession start. Currently elevated but well below 2008 levels. Card + CRE driving recent increase; mortgage charge-offs remain very low (mortgage credit standards strict post-GFC).

rics.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, Real estate loans, commercial
rics.meaning: CRE 30-day delinquency rate. Office sector driving elevation post-2022.
rics.how_to_use: Watch alongside CMBS spreads + special-servicing transfers. CRE loan defaults are slow-moving (loans don't reset until refinancing); the wave of 2024-26 maturities is the test.

rics.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, agricultural loans
rics.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, agricultural loans — share of ag loans 30+ days past due. Leading indicator for charge-offs (charge-offs follow delinquencies by 6-12 months).
rics.how_to_use: Watch for ag-cycle stress. Sustained rise above 2% historically signals farm-credit downturn. Crop prices (corn, soybean, wheat) drive farmer cash flow — track alongside USDA crop forecasts.

rics.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, commercial and industrial loans
rics.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, commercial and industrial loans — share of C&I loans 30+ days past due. Leading indicator of corporate-credit cycle.
rics.how_to_use: Pre-recession warning: rising delinquencies precede rising charge-offs by 6-12 months. Currently elevated but below 2008 peak. SLOOS lending standards typically lead delinquencies by 1-2 quarters.

rics.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, consumer loans, all
rics.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, consumer loans (all) — share of consumer loans 30+ days past due. Comprehensive consumer-credit-stress gauge.
rics.how_to_use: Pre-2008 norm ~3-3.5%; 2008-09 peaked ~5%; post-recovery ~2%. Currently rising from 2022 lows as student-loan resumption + auto-loan stress feed through. Watch alongside subcategory delinquency rates for stress source.

rics.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, consumer loans, credit cards
rics.meaning: Credit card 30-day delinquency rate. Most pro-cyclical loan category.
rics.how_to_use: Crossing 3% historically signals recession risk; now ~3.2% in 2024. Subprime card delinquencies are running much higher (~7%+). Watch alongside disposable income growth — delinquencies rise when real DPI growth turns negative.

rics.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, consumer loans, other
rics.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, consumer loans (other) — auto + personal loans + other non-card consumer credit. Excludes credit cards (separate series) and mortgages.
rics.how_to_use: Auto-loan-driven mostly. Subprime auto delinquencies are the leading edge — rising ahead of broader consumer stress. Track alongside aUSBCLCOOQ/A (charge-offs) for the full credit-cycle.

rics.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, leases
rics.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, leases — equipment lease delinquencies. Smaller portfolio than C&I loans (~$120B at large banks).
rics.how_to_use: Cyclical with capex cycles. Equipment leases (cars, trucks, machinery) become delinquent in slowdowns when small businesses fail. Watch alongside C&I delinquencies for full business-credit-quality picture.

rics.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, real estate loans, all
rics.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, real estate loans (all) — combines residential mortgages + CRE delinquencies.
rics.how_to_use: Aggregate housing-finance stress gauge. CRE-driven recently (office sector); residential delinquencies very low post-Dodd-Frank QM rules. Decompose into residential vs CRE for clean signal.

rics.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, real estate loans, residential
rics.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, residential real estate loans — single-family + multifamily mortgage delinquencies. Pure residential housing-credit gauge.
rics.how_to_use: Very low post-2010 due to QM rules + locked-in low fixed rates. 2008 peak was ~12%; now ~1.5%. Most US homeowners locked in 3-4% mortgages 2020-21 — virtually no delinquency stress despite rate hikes.

rics.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, total loans and leases
rics.meaning: Total Bank Loan Delinquency Rate. Earlier-stage stress signal than charge-offs.
rics.how_to_use: Watch alongside SLOOS lending standards. Delinquencies rising while standards tightening = rough cycle (banks defensive but borrowers still struggling).

rics.description: All Loans, Foreclosures Started
rics.meaning: All loans, foreclosures started — share of mortgages entering foreclosure during the period. MBA quarterly National Delinquency Survey.
rics.how_to_use: Most-direct mortgage-stress gauge. Pre-2008 ~0.5%; peaked ~1.5% in 2009; post-recovery ~0.2%. Currently very low. Track alongside FHA/VA-specific foreclosure rates (higher stress) for credit-tier breakdown.

rics.description: All Loans, Total Past Due
rics.meaning: All loans, total past due — share of mortgages 30+ days delinquent. Aggregate mortgage-credit-quality gauge from MBA.
rics.how_to_use: Sum of 30/60/90+-day delinquencies. Cyclical: rises in recessions, falls in expansions. Currently low (~3.5%) reflecting structural low-rate-locked-in protection. 2008 peak was ~10%.

rics.description: All loans in foreclosure at end of quarter
rics.meaning: All loans in foreclosure at end of quarter.
rics.how_to_use: Stock of in-process foreclosures. Plummeted with strong housing market.

rics.description: All loans, 30 days past due
rics.meaning: All loans, 30 days past due — early-stage mortgage delinquency. Most mortgages in this bucket cure (return to current) within 60 days.
rics.how_to_use: First sign of stress; cure rates ~70%. Watch the 30→60 progression rate as the meaningful credit-stress signal. Currently ~2% (vs ~5% peak in 2009).

rics.description: All loans, 60 days past due
rics.meaning: All loans, 60 days past due — mid-stage mortgage delinquency. Cure rates lower than 30-day (~40%); higher likelihood of progression to 90+ or foreclosure.
rics.how_to_use: Track for credit-cycle escalation. The 30→60 progression rate is a leading indicator of foreclosure starts. Currently ~0.7%.

rics.description: All loans, 90 days past due
rics.meaning: All loans, 90+ days past due — late-stage mortgage delinquency. High probability of foreclosure absent loan modification or short sale.
rics.how_to_use: Most-watched mortgage-stress bucket. Currently ~0.8% (vs 5% peak in 2010). Sustained increase signals housing-credit cycle turning.

rics.description: Loans Serviced, all
rics.meaning: Total Loans Serviced — number of mortgages being administered by servicers. Tracks mortgage-servicing industry size.
rics.how_to_use: Servicing rights are valuable assets; track for servicing-industry consolidation patterns. Slows when refinance activity is low (no new originations being serviced).

rics.description: MBA Mortgage Applications, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: MBA Mortgage Applications week-over-week change — composite of purchase + refinance applications. Released Wednesdays for the prior week.
rics.how_to_use: Highest-frequency mortgage-demand gauge. Refinance index spikes on rate drops; purchase index follows housing-market activity. Pair with the rate level (aUSMGAR) for the rate-vs-volume relationship.

rics.description: MBA Purchase Index
rics.meaning: MBA Purchase Index — weekly mortgage-purchase application volume. Pure home-purchase demand gauge (excludes refinance).
rics.how_to_use: Better real-estate-demand gauge than headline MBA index. Falls before existing home sales (purchase apps lead closings by 30-60 days). Currently weak as elevated rates suppress purchase demand.

rics.description: Mortgage Market Index
rics.meaning: MBA Mortgage Market Index — composite of purchase + refinance volumes. Headline mortgage-application gauge.
rics.how_to_use: Volatile due to refi-rate-sensitivity. Refi spikes (when rates drop sharply) drive index moves but matter less for housing-market activity than purchase apps. Decompose to purchase + refi for clean signal.

rics.description: Mortgage Refinance Index
rics.meaning: MBA Mortgage Refinance Index — weekly refinance application volume. Highly rate-sensitive: 50bp drop in rates can drive 50% spike in this index.
rics.how_to_use: Refi applications signal household interest in lowering payments. Most-locked-in borrowers from 2020-21 lows have no incentive to refi until rates fall toward 5%. Currently very low.

rics.description: Mortgage applications, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Mortgage applications week-over-week change — same conceptual measure as aUSMGAAQ. Cross-check series.
rics.how_to_use: Use whichever is fresher. The MBA index is the standard benchmark for high-frequency mortgage activity.

rics.description: Mortgage applications, conventional market index, refinancing
rics.meaning: MBA Conventional Mortgage Market Index, refinance — refinance applications for conventional (non-government-insured) mortgages.
rics.how_to_use: Conventional-borrower-segment refinance gauge. Cleaner signal than total refi (excludes FHA/VA streamline programs which have different drivers).

rics.description: Mortgage applications, government market index, refinancing
rics.meaning: MBA Government Mortgage Market Index, refinance — refinance applications for government-insured (FHA/VA/USDA) mortgages.
rics.how_to_use: Government-program borrower segment. FHA streamline refi is rate-sensitive even at small rate drops because FHA is a fixed-spread market. Useful for tracking lower-credit-quality borrower behavior.

rics.description: Mortgage applications, market composite index
rics.meaning: MBA Mortgage Applications Composite Index — weekly Mortgage Bankers Association survey. Real-time housing-finance demand.
rics.how_to_use: Composite of purchase + refi indices. Most cyclical when refi-driven (rate-cycle bellwether — surges when rates fall). Purchase index is the cleaner housing-demand gauge.

rics.description: Mortgage applications, market composite index, purchase
rics.meaning: MBA Purchase Mortgage Applications Index — purchase only (excludes refi). The cleanest housing-demand-side gauge.
rics.how_to_use: Leads existing home sales by 1-2 months. Less rate-sensitive than refi but still rate-driven. Affordability (aUSHAI) drives multi-quarter trends.

rics.description: Mortgage applications, market composite index, refinancing
rics.meaning: MBA Refinance Mortgage Applications Index. Highly rate-sensitive — surges when rates fall ~50bp from local peak.
rics.how_to_use: Refi waves are the canonical mortgage-rate-cycle indicator. Most outstanding mortgages have low locked-in rates (pre-2022 issuance), so refi index requires rates to fall well below 6% to reactivate.
